hepb.remark: ECDC general: 2, 4 and 6-18 months. The birth dose is only for babies of HBsAg-positive or unknown-status mothers (risk group), so it is not scheduled. Available from 2000: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, hepatitis B, first year "Yes").

rotavirus.remark: Both rotavirus vaccines are in the Greek programme: RV1 (2 doses, months 2 and 4) and RV5 (3 doses, months 2, 4, 6) (ECDC footnote; WHO immunization data portal, vaccine schedule data (2025 snapshot)); no usage split was found. The generic code and the two doses common to both are used. Available from 2011: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, rotavirus).

dtap.remark: ECDC general: 2, 4, 6, 15-18 months and 4-6 years. Available from 2002: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, acellular pertussis).

hib.remark: ECDC general: 2, 4, 6 and 15-18 months. Available from 2000: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, Hib).

pcv.remark: ECDC: PCV15 or PCV20 at 2, 4 and 12 months; the generic CVX code covers both. Available from 2006: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, PCV).

code.display: Pneumococcal conjugate PCV20, polysaccharide CRM197 conjugate, adjuvant, PF

pcv20.remark: ECDC general: PCV20 from 65 years. Available from 2023: Greek Ministry of Health update of 7 February 2023 recommending PCV20 for adults 65+ (as reported in Frontiers in Public Health, 2023).

ipv.remark: ECDC general: 2, 4, 6-18 months, 4-6 years, and the 18-25 year booster (Tdap-IPV). Available from 2003: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, IPV).

flu.remark: ECDC general: yearly from 60 years. Available from 2007: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, seasonal influenza).

flu_child.remark: ECDC footnote: flu vaccination is recommended to all children 6 months to 5 years since 2024. The pediatric formulation code is used for children.

mmr.remark: ECDC general: 12-15 months and 2-3 years (2017 temporary recommendation). Available from 1995: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, mumps, rubella and second measles dose all from 1995).

var.remark: ECDC general: 12-15 months and 2-3 years. Available from 2008: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, varicella).

hepa.remark: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine schedule data (2025 snapshot), Greece: dose 1 at 2-6 years and dose 2 six months later (general); ECDC shows one window for the first dose. Available from 2017: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, hepatitis A: regional from 2007, national from 2017).

men_b.remark: ECDC general: 2-3, 4-5 and 12-15 months (MenB-4C infant schedule). Available from 2024: inferred: a 2024 ISPOR abstract still describes MenB as high-risk only and the Ministry of Health published a rationale for infant MenB vaccination on 7 August 2024; WHO lists it as routine in 2025.

men_c.remark: ECDC footnote: 1 dose of MenC at 10 months. Available from 2014: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, meningococcal vaccines, any strain).

men.remark: ECDC general: MenACWY at 11-12 years. Available from 2014: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, meningococcal vaccines, any strain).

tdap.remark: ECDC general: 11-12 years, and a booster at 18-25 years. Available from 2002: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, acellular pertussis from 2002); the year of the adolescent and adult Tdap was not found.

code.display: Td (adult), 5 Lf tetanus toxoid, preservative free, adsorbed

td.remark: ECDC footnote: after the 18-25 year booster, Td or Tdap every 10 years. Available from 2002: earliest year of the Greek diphtheria-tetanus booster in the WHO data; no introduction year found.

hpv.remark: ECDC general: 9-11 years, 2-dose scheme with a 6-month interval (footnote 19). Available from 2009: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, HPV; the vaccine was not the 9-valent one at first, and girls only until the 2022 recommendation for boys and girls, neither of which is modelled).

zoster.remark: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine schedule data (2025 snapshot), Greece: dose 1 from 60 years, dose 2 two to six months later (the start of that range is used). Available from 2023: Greek National Vaccination Committee rationale for herpes zoster vaccination, July 2023 (Ministry of Health); the recombinant vaccine was authorised in the EU on 21 March 2018 (EMA).

rsv.remark: Greek National Vaccination Committee, September 2024: one dose, no booster, for everyone aged 75 and over (also for people 60+ with listed risk conditions, which is not modelled); it names two products (Arexvy, Abrysvo) without choosing one, so the generic CVX code is used. ECDC lists RSV as a general recommendation from 75 years. Available from 2025: WHO immunization data portal, vaccine introduction data (Greece, RSV immunization strategy first "Yes" in 2025; the committee's rationale dates from 2024).
